tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

=====NOTES.TXT=====
northstar triage - working notes

Client - Northstar

what we're building
-------------------
service that takes northstar service request (POST /cases/process + X-Event-ID header),
gathers evidence from northstar's systems, and returns the correct FIRST action as a structured
case result. create a work order only when it's safe and fully supported.
contract = case-input.schema.json in, 
case-result.schema.json out. 
GET /health must return 200.

not "faster", it's "faster to the CORRECT first action".
a fast wrong acknowledgement costs more than a slightly slower right one. optimise for that.
do not chase automation rate - make it useful to a coordinator on a busy shift.

who owns what
-------------
- meera (northstar ops) - operating priorities, safety + entitlement calls
- nikhil (northstar IT) - API access, test env, event delivery, X-Event-ID, repeats
- aditi (celeco) - model gateway access/limits, coordination on celeco side
- rohan (northstar) - dispatch practice + coordinator desk. replied 6 oct, owns the three
  dispatch questions. sent OPS-INTAKE-003 + OPS-DISPATCH-004. open q back to him: scheduling
  lead time (see D2 below)

source docs (in docs/client/) - build follows these, not anyone's summary of them:
- POL-SAFETY-001 safety escalation policy
- POL-CONTRACT-002 contract interpretation standard
- OPS-INTAKE-003 request intake + duplicate handling (new, from rohan)
- OPS-DISPATCH-004 technician dispatch standard (new, from rohan)
- SYS-CATALOG-001 northstar systems & API reference
- CELECO-MODEL-001 model gateway guide

constraints / must-knows
------------------------
safety (POL-SAFETY-001 + meera)
- triggers: suspected fuel/gas leak, smoke, water near electrical equipment, anyone dizzy/unwell
  in an equipment room -> immediate human escalation
- in those cases: NO troubleshooting advice, NO automatic work order / dispatch
- keep the customer's exact trigger words in the record, not a generic label
- don't wait to resolve customer/site/asset before escalating
- reporter explicitly says no smoke/smell/water/risk -> normal triage (alarm, loss of cooling,
  noise, failed start are not automatically hazards)
- ambiguous signal -> ask ONE concise safety question, nothing progresses until answered
  (agreed with meera). question must be plain, answerable by whoever is next to the equipment,
  not a form.
- reply "not sure" or no reply -> stays with a human, never drifts back to normal triage
- hazard word in the reply = fresh credible signal, not a resolution
- only the duty owner (human) releases an escalated case back to triage, never the automation
- my two design decisions, meera confirmed she wants them kept even at the cost of automation:
    1. unclear whether ambiguous or credible -> go to human
    2. model can't clear a safety signal on its own. hazard-type wording present, or model
       output missing/malformed -> cautious path

my dispatch decisions (mine, not rohan's - flag in SOLUTION.md, revisit with him)
- D1. breakdowns: same-city only. for a BREAKDOWN, a tech counts as available only if
  qualified + available + tech.city == site.city. none -> resource_escalation_required.
  rohan's actual practice is softer (can they reach it inside the response window, travel as a
  tie-breaker) but that needs travel-time/route/traffic data we don't have and the API doesn't
  give. he does say a distant tech is usually the wrong answer for a tight response term, so
  same-city is the defensible approximation of his rule, and it fails safe (escalates to a
  human rather than promising a visit we can't make).
  deliberately NOT applied to planned work - rohan says travel is fine there because the route
  and day get planned around it.
  cost: AST-701 and AST-1301 drop to a single available tech (TECH-13) once TECH-07/Mysuru and
  TECH-12/Tumakuru are excluded. accepted.
  can't implement his real tie-breakers either: "local familiarity with the site" would need
  tech-to-past-WO history, and work-order-history has no technicianId field. note as a limit.
- D2. planned acknowledgement promises no date. name the service + asset, say the visit is
  being scheduled against the contract, don't commit to a date, slot or window. rohan wants a
  date by which we'd come back with a proposed slot, but we have no data on northstar's
  scheduling lead time and inventing an interval would be exactly the kind of guess the rest
  of this design refuses. a coordinator supplies it.
  the coordinator fills the date in when they pick up the case - OPS-INTAKE-003 already says
  the acknowledgement states what happens next and what's still needed, which this satisfies.

contract / entitlement (POL-CONTRACT-002 + meera)
- coverage comes from the agreement records, not from what the customer says. payment
  receipts, "we're premium", account manager messages = context, not evidence
- decision order: resolve customer + asset first -> find agreement in force by effective dates
  and status -> apply latest dated amendment -> check service mode
- later amendment overrides conflicting base terms, only for what it changes, only from its
  effective date. doesn't rewrite unrelated clauses
- this is where they get hurt most - coordinators quoted response window off base contract
  when an amendment had already changed it
- remote-only service mode does NOT authorise onsite dispatch
- expired / suspended / missing agreement, or conflicts with request -> account review
- payment receipt doesn't reactivate a suspended account until commercial ops allocates it
- newly installed asset isn't covered just because the customer is on a premium plan
- customer/asset/amendment can't be established confidently -> account review before dispatch
- keep as evidence: customer/site/asset used, contract ref + amendment that changed the term,
  reason for human review
- customer reply: coverage clear -> state next action + response window, no internal notes.
  under review -> acknowledge the issue, don't promise attendance, say we're checking the
  account record

identity / missing info (meera + rohan)
- missing equipment details go back to customer or account owner, never guessed
  ("backup unit near pharmacy" story - two similar assets, don't pick one)
- NEW (rohan): customers appear under legal AND trading names. match on aliases[] as well as
  name. they once recreated a job because request 1 was logged under the legal name and
  request 2 under the trading name and nobody saw it was the same site. that's the failure
  mode to design against. data backs this - every customer record has an aliases[] array

duplicates (meera + nikhil + rohan/OPS-INTAKE-003) - now THREE things:
- same X-Event-ID delivered again (at-least-once delivery) -> transport repeat, return the
  original result, never a second work order
- different request about the same job (email + portal 4 mins apart) -> duplicate_detected,
  acknowledge as duplicate, preserve original references, don't open a second WO
- NEW: it turns on the FAULT, not the asset. same fault reported again, or more detail on
  something already open -> link to the existing WO + update it, no second WO. coordinator
  then decides if the existing job needs escalating/reassigning. a genuinely DIFFERENT fault
  on the same asset -> its own WO (skills, parts, coverage can differ; merging hides one of
  the two problems)
- NEW: unclear whether it's a duplicate -> hold for operator review. a human decides. don't
  guess in either direction
- NEW: keep the original request refs linked even when no new WO is created, so the next
  coordinator can see the portal ticket and the email are one incident
- rohan's watch-list: same incident via two channels, forwarded email with a changed subject,
  a second person at the customer reporting the same thing
- compare customer, site, asset, symptoms AND timing before opening another case

work orders (meera + nikhil + API ref + rohan/OPS-DISPATCH-004)
- straight-through only when customer, site, asset, entitlement AND technician match are all
  supported by evidence and nothing consequential is uncertain. everything else -> coordinator
  with reason + evidence attached
- safety cases, uncertain identity/entitlement, out-of-coverage dispatch -> always human
- NEW (rohan): PLANNED WORK IS NOT DISPATCHED AT INTAKE. quarterly/preventive service gets
  scheduled first - coordinator confirms customer/site/asset, checks the contract covers that
  service for that asset, then books a slot that fits the visit window + the tech's route. the
  WO is created when the visit goes on the schedule, NOT at intake.
  why: raising WOs at intake fills the board with open orders sitting for weeks (open-order
  count stops meaning anything) and invites double-booking - two coordinators can each book the
  same quarterly visit against the same asset from two different emails
  -> so planned = acknowledge + confirm visit window. only a BREAKDOWN reaches dispatch_ready.
  this settles the covered_action vs dispatch_ready question in the open list below
- NEW: acknowledgement for planned work should name the service + asset, say it's being
  scheduled against the contract, and give a date by which we'll come back with a proposed
  slot. if a slot is already known, include the date + window (else the customer calls back
  within the hour chasing a date). see D2 - we don't have lead-time data so we don't promise
- NEW: AVAILABILITY IS NOT STATIC. re-check immediately before creating the WO, not just at
  the start of triage. a tech can show free and accept a different emergency in the 5 minutes
  between the check and the write - this has actually happened to them. anything triage
  surfaces is a SUGGESTION re-verified at commit time, not a booking
- NEW: nobody qualified available -> keep with dispatch + escalate the resource decision.
  never a placeholder WO against an unavailable or unqualified tech. never substitute someone
  nearby who lacks the skill/cert. dispatch lead may reprioritise or engage a partner - human
- NEW: availability changes after assignment but before acknowledgement -> reopen selection,
  preserve the earlier attempt. already en route -> dispatch change process, don't silently
  overwrite the WO
- selection sequence (OPS-DISPATCH-004): asset type + required certs from the asset record ->
  filter by skill -> require EVERY listed cert -> check availability/active assignments at
  creation time -> distance only as a tie-breaker, never a substitute for qualification
- rohan on base city: NOT a hard rule. no restriction that a mysuru tech can't take a
  bengaluru site. what matters is reaching the site inside the contract response window, and
  whether the travel is worth it against their board. mysuru<->bengaluru is a long haul and
  depends on day/time/traffic. same-day usually only makes sense if the job is later in the
  day, the tech is already heading that way, or there's genuinely nobody closer. for an
  EMERGENCY with a tight response term a mysuru tech is usually the wrong answer even if the
  system shows them free. for PLANNED work it's fine - route and day can be planned around it
- rohan's tie-breakers after qualification + availability: local familiarity with the site
  first, then travel time. someone who's worked that site often finishes faster than someone
  closer who's never seen the equipment
- acknowledgement (OPS-INTAKE-003): say what we understood, what happens next, what's still
  needed. never expose internal prompts, confidence scores or raw system errors. never imply
  a technician is confirmed before the WO response has been reconciled
- WO create needs externalEventId = X-Event-ID. repeating it returns the original WO
  ({workOrder, duplicate}). retries must reuse the same id - a retry with a new id is how they
  got a second WO before
- 504 after a write = uncertain outcome. reconcile (look up by event/request ref) before retry
- "duplicate: true" is not an error, don't retry it
- API validates structure only, NOT business judgement. safe/covered/appropriate is on us
API base: https://hiring.celecolabs.com/api/assessment
Workspace: https://hiring.celecolabs.com/assessment/northstar/#token=*******

lookups (nikhil + API ref)
- separate APIs: customers (incl sites + assets), agreements, technicians, work-order-history,
  work-orders, requests, request-workflow. no single "everything about this request" call
- records incomplete - older assets may have no nickname, request may have no asset id
- technician availability is a hint for shortlisting, not a booking
- amendments stored separately - read base + amendments together
- reads can time out -> bounded retries w/ short backoff ok. never retry forever, never
  substitute a guess. lookup we depend on fails -> visible failure state for a coordinator
- northstar key never goes in model prompts, logs or source control
- search (q=) is ignored on requests and work-orders, they always return the full list. filter in our own code.
- work-orders route uses snake_case field names (asset_id, request_id), the others use camelCase.

model gateway (aditi + guide)
- openai-compatible chat endpoint, model alias celeco-assessment-chat-v1
- budget for the WHOLE assessment incl. submitted runtime: 300 requests, 1M input tokens,
  150k output tokens. max 30 msgs / 60k chars per request, 2048 output tokens
- text only, no tool calling, optional json-object response format, temp 0-1
- evaluator checks structured behaviour + observed side effects, not exact wording
- test malformed/incomplete output, timeouts, non-deterministic wording

things noticed in the data
--------------------------
- search "Aster" returns 2 different customers (Aster Warehousing CUS-012, Aster Clinical
  Services CUS-019), both in whitefield. customer record has no email field -> can't identify
  by name alone. asset ID → site → customer have to agree, otherwise uncertain identity
- asset carries contractRef + requiredCertifications -> keys for the next lookups
- agreement CON-012-A2: supersedes CON-012, effective 2026-08-12 to 2027-07-31, onsite,
  4h response. amendment points back to base, base doesn't point forward. there's no A1 and no base record. Pick the one agreement valid on receivedAt
- runner cases != visible-cases.json (different customers/assets). hidden cases will differ
  again -> nothing hardcoded to examples
  - request before amendment's start date → account review
  - contract comes from the equipment's own contractRef; check the customer matches.

approach
--------
split the work: model READS, code DECIDES.
- model: one call per case, turns messy text into structured facts (asset/site mentions,
  safety signal affirmed/denied/ambiguous/absent + exact quote, intent, referenced requests)
- code: applies the policy rules to those facts + looked-up records. rules are written from
  the policies, not from test cases, so new phrasings still work (model handles language)
  and decisions stay explainable/testable
- one model call per case also fits the 300 request budget
why? token limit less for testing, design choices vary from budget to budget
endpoint: https://hiring.celecolabs.com/api/assessment?route=model
Allowance: 300 requests, 1000000 input tokens and 150000 output tokens.
Refer:northstar-case-triage\resources\celeco-model-gateway-guide.pdf

pipeline
--------
1. intake - validate input, X-Event-ID already processed? return stored result
2. read - single model call -> facts json. validate. broken/timeout -> cautious path
3. evidence - customer (name + aliases) -> site -> asset -> agreement family in force on
   receivedAt -> qualified + available technicians -> open work orders on the asset.
   bounded retries, failure -> failed
4. decide - in order: safety -> identity -> duplicate (same fault? different fault? unclear
   -> human) -> coverage -> PLANNED vs BREAKDOWN -> technician -> status + reasons
5. act - planned: acknowledge + schedule, NO work order. breakdown: re-check availability
   immediately before the write, then create WO keyed on X-Event-ID. handle duplicate flag,
   reconcile after 504
6. respond - build case result. customer draft by status (templates, no advice on safety cases),
   audit with source refs (policy ids, record ids), model trace ids, warnings

open / to verify in sandbox
---------------------------
- RESOLVED (rohan, 6 oct) covered_action vs dispatch_ready - my reading was right and the
  reason is operational, not contractual. planned work is scheduled, not dispatched: the WO is
  raised when the visit goes on the schedule, not at intake. so covered_action = covered
  planned work (scheduled service, coverage confirmation), dispatch_ready = covered BREAKDOWN
  + tech matched + WO created. the discriminator is planned vs breakdown, NOT coverage and NOT
  technician availability. data agrees: VIS-001 is covered and has an available tech
  (TECH-01/08) and still expects covered_action
- RESOLVED (data) what the base CON-012 says vs A2, does an A1 exist - neither exists. 13
  agreements, one per customer, no base contracts, no intermediate amendments. q=CON-012
  returns only CON-012-A2. CON-044-A3 exists with no A1/A2 and no supersedes. see FINDINGS.md
- PARTLY RESOLVED how a business duplicate is found when the earlier request didn't create a
  WO - NOT via saved workflow state: workflow is null on all 18 seeded requests including the
  VIS-001 that VIS-005 duplicates. so it's route=requests (full list, filter client-side -
  q= is ignored there) + our own store. rohan adds the matching rule: compare customer, site,
  asset, symptoms, timing, and decide same-fault vs different-fault
- still open: should we write to request-workflow (coordinator workspace) for non-dispatch
  cases? likely part of "useful to a coordinator" + possibly an observed side effect. check.
  OPS-INTAKE-003 "record the decision" leans yes
- still open: submission.json manifest schema - haven't found it yet

deliverables
------------
README.md, Dockerfile, SOLUTION.md, AI_WORKLOG.md, agent-sessions/, QUALITY.md, submission.json
QUALITY.md needs: visible runner results + own tests for uncertainty, retry, safety,
malformed model output. method, results, known limits.
known limit already: "no reply" to a safety question can't be seen by a request-driven service.

housekeeping
------------
- keys only in .env (gitignored). redact cel_northstar_ / cel_model_ anywhere in logs before commit
- keep every agent session, index in AI_WORKLOG.md

=====CLAUDE.md=====
# Northstar case triage — working rules

Takes one Northstar service request, returns the correct **first action**. A fast wrong
acknowledgement costs more than a slightly slower right one. Never optimise for automation rate.

## Hard rules

1. **Safety first, and it wins.** Hazard signal (fuel/gas leak, smoke, water near electrical
   equipment, anyone dizzy/unwell in an equipment room) → `human_escalation_required`. No
   troubleshooting, no work order, no dispatch. Escalate before resolving customer/site/asset.
2. **The model can never clear a safety signal.** Hazard wording, or model output
   missing/malformed/timed out → cautious path. Ambiguous → ask ONE plain safety question
   (`clarification_required`), progress nothing. "Not sure"/no reply stays with a human.
   Only a human duty owner releases an escalated case.
3. **Preserve the customer's exact trigger words.** Never a generic label.
4. **No work order unless fully evidenced.** Customer, site, asset, entitlement AND technician
   all supported by records, nothing consequential uncertain. Else → coordinator, with reason
   and evidence. **Planned work is never dispatched at intake** (OPS-DISPATCH-004): a covered
   planned service → acknowledge + schedule, no WO; the WO is raised when the visit is placed
   on the schedule. Only a breakdown reaches `dispatch_ready`.
5. **Coverage comes from agreement records only.** Customer claims, payment receipts and
   account-manager messages are context, never evidence. Remote-only does not authorise onsite
   dispatch. Expired/suspended/missing/conflicting → `account_review_required`. Asset-level
   `coverage` and agreement `serviceMode`/`status` can disagree — the stricter controls.
   Received before the agreement's start date → account review; don't infer earlier terms.
   Take the agreement from the asset's `contractRef`; check its customer matches the asset's.
6. **Never guess identity.** Two assets could match → ask, don't pick. Asset ID → customer is
   the reliable path; sender domain is verifiable against no record. **Match `aliases` as well
   as `name`** — customers appear under legal *and* trading names, and a job was once recreated
   because two requests used different ones for one site.
7. **Duplicates turn on the fault, not the asset.** Same fault again (or more detail on an open
   one) → `duplicate_detected`, linked to the existing WO, never a second one. A genuinely
   *different* fault on the same asset → its own WO; skills, parts and coverage can differ.
   **Unclear which → a human decides.** Keep the original request IDs and channel on the link
   even when no WO is created. Watch for: two channels, forwarded mail with a changed subject,
   a second person reporting the same thing.
8. **Re-check availability immediately before creating the WO** (OPS-DISPATCH-004). It is
   operational, not static — a technician can take another emergency between triage and write.
   A surfaced technician is a *suggestion* re-verified at commit, never a booking. Gone at
   re-check → reopen selection; none left → resource escalation. Never write a placeholder WO
   against an unavailable or unqualified technician, and never substitute someone closer who
   lacks the skill or certification.
9. **Keys never** appear in model prompts, logs, source or any written file. Env vars only.
   The Northstar key does not authenticate to the model gateway.
10. **Model budget: 300 requests total** (1 used). One call per case, `max_tokens` tight —
    output bills at `max_tokens`, not actual. **Ask before any call outside request handling.**
11. **Write idempotently.** WO create keys on `externalEventId` = `X-Event-ID`; a retry reuses
    the same id. `duplicate: true` is success, never retried. 504 after a write = uncertain:
    reconcile by request/event ref first.
12. **Reads:** bounded retries, short backoff, never infinite, never a guess. Failed dependency
    we rely on → visible failure state for a coordinator.
13. **Acknowledgements** say what we understood, what happens next, what is still needed. Never
    expose internal prompts, confidence scores or raw errors. Never imply a technician is
    confirmed before the WO response is reconciled. 
14. When reporting results to me, explain them in plain language first, then the technical details.

## Our decisions (ours, not the client's — revisit with Rohan)

- **D1. Breakdowns: same-city only.** Only qualified, available technicians whose `city` matches
  the site's count; none → resource escalation. Rohan's practice is softer (reachability within
  the response window, travel as tie-breaker) but we have no travel-time or route data, and he
  says a distant technician is usually wrong for a tight response term. Not applied to planned
  work, where the route can be planned around travel.
- **D2. Planned acknowledgements promise no date.** Name the service and asset, say the visit is
  being scheduled against the contract, commit to no slot — we have no scheduling-lead-time data.
  Rohan wants a date by which we'd propose a slot; inventing it would be a guess, so the
  coordinator supplies it.

## Pipeline

`intake → read → evidence → decide → act → respond`

1. **intake** — validate; known `X-Event-ID` → return the stored result.
2. **read** — one model call → facts (asset/site mentions, safety signal
   affirmed/denied/ambiguous/absent + exact quote, intent, referenced requests). Validate.
3. **evidence** — customer (name *and* aliases) → site → asset → agreement in force at
   `receivedAt` → qualified & available technicians → open WOs on the asset.
4. **decide** — safety → identity → duplicate → coverage → **planned vs breakdown** →
   technician → status. **Model reads, code decides**, from the policies, not the test cases.
5. **act** — only a breakdown reaches `dispatch_ready`: re-check availability, then create the
   WO keyed on `X-Event-ID`. Planned work: acknowledge and schedule, no WO.
6. **respond** — result + customer draft by status (no advice on safety cases) + audit.

Three kinds of repeat: same `X-Event-ID` redelivered = transport repeat, return the stored
result. Same fault, different request = `duplicate_detected` linked to the existing WO.
Different fault, same asset = its own WO. An open WO on the asset is **not** on its own a
duplicate — compare customer, site, asset, symptoms and timing.

## Layout

`app/` service code · `tests/` ours + provided runner/schemas · `exploration/` API survey +
FINDINGS.md · `resources/` client PDFs, source of truth over any summary: POL-SAFETY-001,
POL-CONTRACT-002, OPS-INTAKE-003, OPS-DISPATCH-004, SYS-CATALOG-001, CELECO-MODEL-001.

## Run / test

```bash
uvicorn app.main:app --port 8080            # local
pytest -q                                    # tests
docker build -t northstar-triage . && \
  docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 --env-file .env northstar-triage
node tests/celeco-visible-runner.mjs http://localhost:8080
```

Config from environment variables only; `.env` is local dev and gitignored. Keys are passed at
`docker run` time, never baked into the image.

  "properties": {

    "entities": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["customerId", "siteId", "assetId"],
      "properties": { "customerId": { "type": ["string", "null"] }, "siteId": { "type": ["string", "null"] }, "assetId": { "type": ["string", "null"] } }
    },
    "classification": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["category", "urgency", "safetyRisk", "confidence"],
      "properties": { "category": { "type": "string" }, "urgency": { "type": "string" }, "safetyRisk": { "type": "boolean" }, "confidence": { "type": "number", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 1 } }
    },
    "entitlement": { "type": "object", "required": ["status", "sla", "evidence"] },
    "nextActions": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "object", "required": ["type", "reason"] } },
    "customerResponseDraft": { "type": "string" },
    "missingInformation": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" } },
    "workOrder": { "type": ["object", "null"] },
    "audit": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["sourceReferences", "modelTraceIds", "warnings"],
      "properties": { "sourceReferences": { "type": "array" }, "modelTraceIds": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" } }, "warnings": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" } } }
    }
  }
}

- **D2. Planned acknowledgements promise no date.** Name the service and asset, say the visit is
  being scheduled against the contract, commit to no slot — we have no scheduling-lead-time data.
  Rohan wants a date by which we'd propose a slot; inventing it would be a guess, so the
  coordinator supplies it.

## Pipeline

`intake → read → evidence → decide → act → respond`

1. **intake** — validate; known `X-Event-ID` → return the stored result.
2. **read** — one model call → facts (asset/site mentions, safety signal
   affirmed/denied/ambiguous/absent + exact quote, intent, referenced requests). Validate.
3. **evidence** — customer (name *and* aliases) → site → asset → agreement in force at
   `receivedAt` → qualified & available technicians → open WOs on the asset.
4. **decide** — safety → identity → duplicate → coverage → **planned vs breakdown** →
   technician → status. **Model reads, code decides**, from the policies, not the test cases.
5. **act** — only a breakdown reaches `dispatch_ready`: re-check availability, then create the
   WO keyed on `X-Event-ID`. Planned work: acknowledge and schedule, no WO.
6. **respond** — result + customer draft by status (no advice on safety cases) + audit.

Three kinds of repeat: same `X-Event-ID` redelivered = transport repeat, return the stored
result. Same fault, different request = `duplicate_detected` linked to the existing WO.
Different fault, same asset = its own WO. An open WO on the asset is **not** on its own a
duplicate — compare customer, site, asset, symptoms and timing.

## Layout

`app/` service code · `tests/` ours + provided runner/schemas · `exploration/` API survey +
FINDINGS.md · `resources/` client PDFs, source of truth over any summary: POL-SAFETY-001,
POL-CONTRACT-002, OPS-INTAKE-003, OPS-DISPATCH-004, SYS-CATALOG-001, CELECO-MODEL-001.

## Run / test

```bash
uvicorn app.main:app --port 8080            # local
pytest -q                                    # tests
docker build -t northstar-triage . && \
  docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 --env-file .env northstar-triage
node tests/celeco-visible-runner.mjs http://localhost:8080
```

Config from environment variables only; `.env` is local dev and gitignored. Keys are passed at
`docker run` time, never baked into the image.

import sys, zlib, re

def extract(path):
    d = open(path, 'rb').read()
    chunks = []
    for m in re.finditer(rb'stream\r?\n', d):
        s = m.end()
        e = d.find(b'endstream', s)
        if e < 0: continue
        try:
            t = zlib.decompress(d[s:e])
        except Exception:
            continue
        chunks.append(t)
    lines = []
    for t in chunks:
        txt = t.decode('latin-1')
        # find text-showing ops, in order
        for m in re.finditer(r'\[(?P<arr>[^\]]*)\]\s*TJ|\((?P<s>(?:\\.|[^\\()])*)\)\s*Tj|T\*|Td|TD', txt):

                parts = re.findall(r'\((?:\\.|[^\\()])*\)', m.group('arr'))
                lines.append(''.join(p[1:-1] for p in parts))
            elif m.group('s') is not None:
                lines.append(m.group('s'))
            else:

######################### northstar-safety-escalation-policy.pdf #########################


Northstar Field Services 267 Project material

Page 1

NORTHSTAR FIELD SERVICES

Safety escalation policy

SAFETY POLICY

POL-SAFETY-001

Owner: Head of Operations | Effective: 01 July 2026 | Review cycle: quarterly | Applies to email,
portal and coordinator-created requests.

Purpose and operating principle

This standard protects customers, site staff and Northstar technicians when the first report may
indicate an immediate hazard. The service desk is not a remote emergency-diagnosis function. When
the signal is credible, speed means escalating cleanly, preserving evidence and avoiding advice that
could increase exposure.

Immediate escalation

Reports involving a suspected fuel or gas leak, smoke, water near electrical equipment, or people
feeling dizzy or unwell in an equipment room require immediate human escalation.

The intake system must not provide troubleshooting instructions or create an automatic dispatch for
these cases. It should preserve the original report, identify the safety signal and route the case to the
duty owner.

Required first action

177 Keep people away from the affected area and preserve the customer222s original wording.

177 Mark the request for immediate human review.

177 Do not diagnose the fault, offer repair instructions or create a work order automatically.

What is not automatically a safety escalation

An equipment alarm, loss of cooling, unusual noise or failed start is not automatically an immediate
hazard when the reporter explicitly confirms there is no smoke, smell, water, exposed electrical
equipment or person at risk. Those requests still need normal triage. If the description is ambiguous,
ask one concise safety question before progressing.

Northstar Field Services 267 Project material

Page 2

Minimum escalation record

177 Original request ID, channel, sender and received time.

177 The exact words that triggered the escalation; do not replace them with a generic label.

177 Customer, site and asset if confidently known. Do not delay escalation to resolve them.

177 Who was notified, when, and whether the customer acknowledged the safety instruction.

Examples

Escalate: a guard reports diesel odour and a wet patch below a generator; staff feel light-headed in a
closed plant room; water is collecting beside an electrical panel; smoke is visible from an equipment
enclosure.

Continue normal triage: a compressor is losing pressure with no heat, smell or leak reported; an
HVAC unit is noisy but cooling; a generator fails a scheduled start test and the site confirms there is
no immediate hazard.

Exception handling

If later information clears the immediate hazard, the duty owner - not the intake automation - releases
the request back to standard triage. The audit record keeps both the original signal and the release
decision.

Shared by Northstar Field Services for this engagement.

######################### northstar-request-intake-standard.pdf #########################


Northstar Field Services 267 Project material

Page 1

NORTHSTAR FIELD SERVICES

Request intake and duplicate handling

OPERATIONS STANDARD

OPS-INTAKE-003

Owner: Dispatch Lead | Effective: 15 July 2026 | Covers email, portal and staff-created requests.

Why the process exists

The intake record is the chain of evidence from a customer's words to Northstar's first action. The
coordinator may move back and forth between records while waiting for answers; the workflow below
is a decision checklist, not a claim that every request arrives neatly.

Current intake process

177 Open the request and preserve the sender, channel, time and attachments.

177 Resolve the customer, site and asset from the message and account records. Ask the customer

when a material identifier is missing.

177 Check for safety language before troubleshooting or dispatch.

177 Check the active contract and any later amendments.

177 Search recent requests and work orders for the same incident.

177 Choose the next action: request information, route for approval, escalate, or prepare a dispatch.

177 Record the decision and send the customer a clear acknowledgement.

Duplicate reports

Customers sometimes report one incident through email and the portal. Intake should compare the
customer, site, asset, symptoms and timing before opening another case.

An exact retry of a work-order request must return the original work order. It must not create another
record. A similar report should be linked to the existing incident or held for operator review when the
match is uncertain.

Every accepted request keeps its original request ID and channel for audit.

Northstar Field Services 267 Project material

Page 2

Minimum information by outcome

Clarification: record what cannot be resolved and ask only for information that changes the next
action. Safety escalation: preserve the original wording and duty-owner handoff. Account review:
retain the agreement evidence and uncertainty. Dispatch: retain identity, safety, entitlement, resource
and idempotency evidence.

Idempotency and retries

Each work-order creation uses an external event ID that remains stable across retries. If the
response is lost, query the work-order service using the request or event reference before trying
again. A new event ID for the same attempt can create an operational duplicate.

Customer acknowledgements

The acknowledgement should say what Northstar understood, what will happen next and what
information is still needed. It must not expose internal prompts, confidence scores or raw system
errors. Never imply that a technician is confirmed before the work-order response has been
reconciled.

Shared by Northstar Field Services for this engagement.


######################### northstar-contract-interpretation-standard.pdf #########################


Northstar Field Services 267 Project material

Page 1

NORTHSTAR FIELD SERVICES

Contract interpretation standard

COMMERCIAL STANDARD

POL-CONTRACT-002

Owner: Head of Operations with Commercial Operations | Effective: 01 August 2026 | Applies before
any commitment to attend site.

Purpose

Northstar uses the service agreement to decide what the customer is entitled to, the response
commitment and whether an on-site visit can be authorised. Customer language, payment advice and
account-manager messages are useful context but do not replace the current agreement record.

Coverage and amendments

Coverage is determined from the active service contract together with its dated amendments.

When a later amendment conflicts with the base contract, the later amendment controls. If the
customer, asset or applicable amendment cannot be established confidently, the case requires
account review before dispatch.

Evidence to retain

177 The customer, site and asset used for the coverage decision.

177 The active contract reference and any later amendment that changed the applicable term.

177 The reason for human review when the records do not support a confident decision.

Northstar Field Services 267 Project material

Page 2

Decision order

177 Resolve the customer and asset before interpreting coverage.

177 Find the current agreement by its effective dates and status.

177 Apply the latest dated amendment when it supersedes an earlier schedule or term.

177 Check the service mode. Remote-only support does not authorise an on-site dispatch.

177 Use account review when the agreement is expired, suspended, missing, or conflicts with the

request.

Common exceptions

A payment receipt does not reactivate a suspended account until Commercial Operations allocates it.
A newly installed asset is not covered merely because the customer has a premium plan. An
amendment may add equipment or change a response term from its effective date; it does not rewrite
unrelated clauses.

Customer communication

When coverage is clear, state the next action and the applicable response window without quoting
internal notes. When review is needed, acknowledge the operational issue, avoid promising
attendance, and tell the customer that Northstar is checking the account record.

Shared by Northstar Field Services for this engagement.

customer, site, asset, symptoms and timing before opening another case.

An exact retry of a work-order request must return the original work order. It must not create another
record. A similar report should be linked to the existing incident or held for operator review when the
match is uncertain.

Every accepted request keeps its original request ID and channel for audit.

Northstar Field Services 267 Project material

Page 2

Minimum information by outcome

Clarification: record what cannot be resolved and ask only for information that changes the next
action. Safety escalation: preserve the original wording and duty-owner handoff. Account review:
retain the agreement evidence and uncertainty. Dispatch: retain identity, safety, entitlement, resource
and idempotency evidence.

Idempotency and retries

Each work-order creation uses an external event ID that remains stable across retries. If the
response is lost, query the work-order service using the request or event reference before trying
again. A new event ID for the same attempt can create an operational duplicate.

Customer acknowledgements

The acknowledgement should say what Northstar understood, what will happen next and what
information is still needed. It must not expose internal prompts, confidence scores or raw system
errors. Never imply that a technician is confirmed before the work-order response has been
reconciled.

Northstar Field Services 267 Project material

Page 1

NORTHSTAR FIELD SERVICES

Contract interpretation standard

COMMERCIAL STANDARD

POL-CONTRACT-002

Owner: Head of Operations with Commercial Operations | Effective: 01 August 2026 | Applies before
any commitment to attend site.

Purpose

Northstar uses the service agreement to decide what the customer is entitled to, the response
commitment and whether an on-site visit can be authorised. Customer language, payment advice and
account-manager messages are useful context but do not replace the current agreement record.

Coverage and amendments

Coverage is determined from the active service contract together with its dated amendments.

When a later amendment conflicts with the base contract, the later amendment controls. If the
customer, asset or applicable amendment cannot be established confidently, the case requires
account review before dispatch.

Evidence to retain

177 The customer, site and asset used for the coverage decision.

177 The active contract reference and any later amendment that changed the applicable term.

177 The reason for human review when the records do not support a confident decision.

Northstar Field Services 267 Project material

Page 2

Decision order

177 Resolve the customer and asset before interpreting coverage.

177 Find the current agreement by its effective dates and status.

177 Apply the latest dated amendment when it supersedes an earlier schedule or term.

177 Check the service mode. Remote-only support does not authorise an on-site dispatch.

177 Use account review when the agreement is expired, suspended, missing, or conflicts with the

request.

Common exceptions

A payment receipt does not reactivate a suspended account until Commercial Operations allocates it.
A newly installed asset is not covered merely because the customer has a premium plan. An
amendment may add equipment or change a response term from its effective date; it does not rewrite
unrelated clauses.

When coverage is clear, state the next action and the applicable response window without quoting
internal notes. When review is needed, acknowledge the operational issue, avoid promising
attendance, and tell the customer that Northstar is checking the account record.

######################### northstar-technician-dispatch-standard.pdf #########################


Northstar Field Services 267 Project material

Page 1

NORTHSTAR FIELD SERVICES

Technician dispatch standard

DISPATCH STANDARD

OPS-DISPATCH-004

Owner: Dispatch Lead | Effective: 15 July 2026 | Availability data is operational and may change
during a shift.

Purpose

This standard governs the final selection made before an on-site work order is created. It deliberately
separates recommendation from dispatch: a coordinator can prepare a likely match, but the final write
must use current qualification and availability evidence.

Qualification and availability

A technician may be dispatched only when their skills and current certifications match the asset and
work required.

Availability must be checked again immediately before work-order creation. If no suitable technician is
available, the request stays with dispatch for a human decision rather than being assigned to the
closest person automatically.

Dispatch record

177 Record the selected technician, the matching skill and the availability check.

177 Keep the request with dispatch when qualification or availability is uncertain.

177 Do not substitute a nearby technician who lacks the required skill or certification.

Northstar Field Services 267 Project material

Page 2

Selection sequence

177 Confirm the asset type and the certification requirements stored on the asset record.

177 Filter for the required skill, then require every listed certification.

177 Check current availability and active assignments immediately before creation.

177 Keep distance as a tie-breaker after qualification, not as a substitute for it.

No suitable resource

If nobody qualified is available, retain the request with dispatch and escalate the resource decision.
Do not create a placeholder work order against an unavailable or unqualified technician. The dispatch
lead may reprioritise another job or engage a partner, but that is a human decision.

Changes after assignment

If availability changes after assignment but before acknowledgement, reopen selection and preserve
the earlier attempt. If the technician is already en route, use the dispatch change process rather than
silently overwriting the work order.

Shared by Northstar Field Services for this engagement.

Northstar systems and API reference

SYSTEMS REFERENCE

SYS-CATALOG-001

Owner: IT Manager | Interface version: 2026-09 | Environment: isolated project workspace.

Operations workspace

Northstar Operations is the coordinator team's working application. It combines email and portal
requests, saves workflow progress and records the customer response. Coordinators still check
evidence across several records before they act.

Authentication

Use the private assessment token as a bearer token. Keep it in an environment variable and never
commit it.

Authorization: Bearer $NORTHSTAR_ACCESS_TOKEN
Base URL: https://hiring.celecolabs.com/api/assessment

Available services

177 GET ?route=requests - requests and saved workflow state.

177 POST ?route=request-workflow - triage, notes and customer reply draft.

177 GET ?route=customers&q;=Aster - customer, site and asset lookup.

177 GET ?route=agreements&q;=CON-012-A2 - service agreement and amendment lookup.

177 GET ?route=technicians - qualifications and current availability.

177 GET ?route=work-order-history&q;=AST-101 - searchable service history.

177 GET or POST ?route=work-orders - active work orders and creation.

Work-order creation

{
"externalEventId": "evt-1042",
"requestId": "REQ-1042",
"assetId": "AST-101",
"technicianId": "TECH-01",
"safetyRisk": false
}

The API validates authentication, required fields, referenced record IDs and idempotency. It behaves
like the current CRM and does not decide whether a dispatch is safe, covered or operationally sound.
Your system owns that judgement. Repeating an accepted externalEventId returns the original work
order.

Northstar Field Services 267 Project material

Page 2

Known limitations

177 Records may be incomplete and a request may not contain an asset identifier.

177 Dependencies can time out, so callers should validate responses and retry safe reads.

177 Technician availability can change between selection and dispatch.

Request and response behaviour

Successful list calls return {results:[...]}. Successful creation returns {workOrder, duplicate}. Validation
errors return HTTP 400 or 422 with an error and reasons. A dependency timeout returns 504. Treat a
timeout after a write as an uncertain outcome: reconcile by request or external event reference before
retrying.

{
"requestId": "REQ-1042",
"status": "awaiting_approval",
"customerId": "CUS-012",
"siteId": "SITE-008",
"assetId": "AST-101",
"safetyOutcome": "clear",
"coverageOutcome": "needs_review",
"technicianId": null,
"coordinatorNotes": "Later amendment needs review",
"customerReplyDraft": "We are checking the account record."
}

Security and isolation

The Northstar key is valid only for Northstar Operations and the business APIs. It will not authenticate
to the Celeco model gateway or the assessment submission service. Do not place it in source control,
browser logs or model prompts.

CELECO LABS

Celeco model gateway guide

ASSESSMENT SERVICE

CELECO-MODEL-001

What Celeco provides

Celeco provides a private OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint for the runtime AI inside your
submission. The gateway keeps the model configuration consistent across candidates. It is separate
from Northstar's Operations account and APIs.

Aditi Rao, Celeco's engagement manager, owns access and support for this gateway. Northstar staff
do not administer it.

Access

Open the Model gateway tab in your T-1 workspace and copy the private access key. Keep it in an
environment variable and never commit it.

Authorization: Bearer $CELECO_MODEL_GATEWAY_KEY
POST https://hiring.celecolabs.com/api/assessment?route=model

Request

{
"model": "celeco-assessment-chat-v1",
"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Classify this request."}],
"temperature": 0,
"max_tokens": 1200
}

The response follows the familiar chat-completions shape. Build against the alias shown above rather
than a provider model name.

Assessment allowance

177 300 requests.

177 1 million input tokens and 150,000 output tokens.

177 Up to 30 messages and 60,000 characters in one request.

177 2,048 maximum output tokens per request.

The allowance is intentionally large enough for development and testing but small enough to reward
deliberate experiments. Reservations are atomic, so simultaneous requests cannot exceed the
assessment cap.

Celeco Labs 267 T-1 assessment service

Page 2

Supported request contract

177 One to 30 system, user or assistant messages.

177 Text content only, with at most 60,000 characters across the request.

177 Temperature from 0 to 1 and an optional JSON-object response format.

177 No provider-specific tools, files, images, embeddings or model names.

Testing advice

Use the gateway while developing and in the submitted runtime. Test malformed or incomplete model
output, timeouts and non-deterministic wording. The evaluator checks structured behaviour and
observed side effects rather than an exact prose match.

Support boundary

Email Aditi for gateway access, limits or failures. Ask Nikhil at Northstar for their internal platform,
data and API access.

===== FINDINGS.md =====
# Exploration findings

Read-only pass over the six Northstar GET routes + one model-gateway probe.
No POST to Northstar. Model budget used: 1 / 300.
Raw responses in `raw/`. Re-run with `node exploration/explore.mjs`.

## Record shapes

**customer** (13, `?route=customers`) — nested, one call gets site + asset:
`{id, name, aliases[], status, sites[{id, customerId, name, city, assets[{id, siteId, type,
nickname, coverage, contractRef, requiredCertifications[]}]}]}`
`status`: active ×12, on_hold ×1 (CUS-074). **No email or domain field anywhere.**

**agreement** (13, `?route=agreements`) — flat:
`{id, customerId, status, serviceMode, responseHours, effectiveFrom, effectiveTo, supersedes?, note?}`
`status`: active ×12, suspended ×1. `serviceMode`: onsite ×12, remote_only ×1.
`responseHours`: 2, 4, 6, 8, 12.

**technician** (13) — `{id, name, city, skills[], certifications[], available, currentAssignment?}`
Cities: Bengaluru ×11, Mysuru ×1, Tumakuru ×1. 8 available / 5 not.

**request** (18, `?route=requests`) — `{id, requestId, receivedAt, channel, priority, sender{name,email},
subject, body, attachments[{id,name,type,summary}], workflow}`
Two fields the POST input schema does NOT carry: `priority` (low/normal/high/urgent) and
`attachments[].summary` (pre-summarised text — no OCR needed). `workflow` is `null` on all 18.

**work order, active** (4, `?route=work-orders`) — **snake_case, unlike every other route**:
`{id, request_id, customer_id, site_id, asset_id, technician_id, status, summary, created_at, source}`

**work-order history** (24) — camelCase:
`{id, requestId, customerId, siteId, assetId, category, summary, status, openedAt, closedAt}`
`status`: completed ×21, closed_after_review ×2, remote_resolution ×1.

## Answers to "open / to verify"

**1. covered_action vs dispatch_ready** — data supports your reading, with a sharper line.
The two `covered_action` runner cases (VIS-001 scheduled quarterly service, VIS-008 coverage
confirmation) are both *planned/administrative* work; `dispatch_ready` (VIS-006) is a
*breakdown* — "has stopped cooling". Discriminator is breakdown-vs-planned, not coverage.
Note VIS-001 is covered, has an available tech (TECH-01/08) and still expects `covered_action`
— so **availability alone must not promote planned work to dispatch**.

**2. How a business duplicate is found** — not via saved workflow state. `workflow` is `null`
on all 18 seeded requests, including VIS-001 which VIS-005 duplicates. So the only evidence
is: (a) `?route=requests` (full list) matched on asset + time proximity + body cross-reference,
and/or (b) the pre-existing open WO. Note the runner POSTs cases in order, so VIS-001 is
processed before VIS-005, but it arrives as a POST — your own store is the reliable record.
**`q=` is ignored on this route** (see traps), so filter client-side.

**3. Writing to request-workflow** — the API ref documents the workflow record and all 18 are
`null`, i.e. nothing has populated them. It is a documented POST and plausibly an observed
side effect, but it is a write and you said no POSTs yet. Fields line up with the case result
(`safetyOutcome`, `coverageOutcome`, `coordinatorNotes`, `customerReplyDraft`). Flagged for
your decision — untested.

**4. What CON-012 base says, does an A1 exist** — **neither exists.** See below; this is the
biggest correction to the notes.

**5. submission.json manifest schema** — not found. Not in the resources, not served by any
read route. Still open; likely in the workspace UI.

## Corrections / additions to the notes

**Agreement "families" do not exist in this data.** Exactly 13 agreements, one per customer,
no base contracts and no intermediate amendments. `q=CON-012` returns only `CON-012-A2`;
`q=CON-129` returns only `CON-129-A1`. CON-044-**A3** exists with no A1/A2 and no `supersedes`.
`supersedes` appears on only 2 of 13 records (CON-012-A2 → CON-012, CON-129-A1 → CON-129) and
points at a record that is **not retrievable**.
Consequence: there is no base-vs-amendment conflict to resolve at runtime — the one in-force
record per customer already carries the final `responseHours` and `serviceMode`. Build
"latest in force by date + status" as a general selector over whatever the family returns
(correct per policy, handles hidden cases), but do **not** make a resolvable base contract a
precondition — a missing `supersedes` target is normal here, not a reason for account review.
VIS-008 ("use the amendment, not the base contract") is satisfied by citing CON-012-A2 and its
4-hour window.

**Identity cannot be resolved by sender domain.** Customer records have no email field, and
`q=` on customers matches **name and aliases only** — `asterwarehousing.in`, `Whitefield`,
`AST-101` and `Main DG` all return 0 results. The Aster collision is real (CUS-012 Aster
Warehousing, CUS-019 Aster Clinical Services, both Bengaluru/Whitefield). In practice the
reliable path is **asset ID → customer**, by fetching customers and indexing assets locally;
asset IDs are globally unique across the dataset. Domain is a corroborating signal at best,
and you cannot verify it against any record.

**`q=` is silently ignored on `requests` and `work-orders`.** Both return the complete list
for any query (18 and 4 respectively) and return HTTP 200 — no error, no empty set. Only
`customers`, `agreements` and `work-order-history` actually filter. Anything that assumes
server-side filtering on those two routes will quietly operate on every record.

**Coverage is carried at asset level too, and can disagree with the agreement.**
`asset.coverage` ∈ premium / standard / suspended / remote_only. Two assets where it matters:
- `AST-801` — `coverage: "suspended"`, under `CON-074` (`status: suspended`, expired
  2026-08-31, `note: "Renewal payment awaiting allocation."`). Matching request REQ-8268 cites
  a bank transfer advice. Both layers agree: account review. This is the payment-receipt trap,
  fully instrumented in the data.
- `AST-901` — `coverage: "remote_only"` under `CON-083-A1` (`serviceMode: "remote_only"`).
  Matching request REQ-8271 explicitly asks for "someone on site". Remote-only must not
  authorise onsite dispatch, so this is the service-mode trap.
Treat the stricter of the two layers as controlling.

**`CON-019` expires 2026-12-31 and `CON-074` already expired** (2026-08-31, before the
2026-09-20 request dates). Date arithmetic must run against `receivedAt`, as you planned.

**Resource escalation has a single clean discriminator.** Computing skill ⊇ asset.type and
certifications ⊇ asset.requiredCertifications across all 22 assets: **AST-205 is the only
asset with zero available qualified technicians** — it needs `["electrical","high-voltage"]`
+ generator, which only TECH-04 satisfies, and TECH-04 is unavailable (on WO-9285). AST-205 is
exactly the runner's VIS-007 case. Everything else has ≥1 available match. Also: TECH-07
(Mysuru) and TECH-12 (Tumakuru) are out-of-city — if you filter on city, AST-701/AST-1301 drop
to a single available tech (TECH-13).

**Pre-existing open work orders overlap the runner's cases.** `WO-9294` is open on AST-101
(created 09:20, `diagnosis_in_progress`) and `WO-9290` is open on AST-302 (`assigned`).
These are the assets in VIS-001/005 (AST-101) and VIS-006 (AST-302) — and VIS-006 is expected
to be `dispatch_ready` **despite an already-open WO on the same asset**. So "open WO on this
asset" is NOT sufficient for `duplicate_detected`; it would break VIS-006. The duplicate
signal has to come from the request referring to the same job (VIS-005 names Kavya's portal
request explicitly), not from asset overlap alone.

**The seeded `requests` store is the runner's dataset, not visible-cases.json.** Seeded
records are VIS-001…VIS-008 with `REQ-V00n` IDs, matching the IDs embedded in
`celeco-visible-runner.mjs`. `visible-cases.json` (DEMO-100n / Orion / Saffron / Vistara) is a
third, different set. Bodies in the store are also *longer* than the runner's POST payloads
(VIS-001 adds "Tuesday morning is preferred"), so don't match requests by exact body text.

===== FINDINGS.md =====
# Exploration findings

Read-only pass over the six Northstar GET routes + one model-gateway probe.
No POST to Northstar. Model budget used: 1 / 300.
Raw responses in `raw/`. Re-run with `node exploration/explore.mjs`.

## Record shapes

**customer** (13, `?route=customers`) — nested, one call gets site + asset:
`{id, name, aliases[], status, sites[{id, customerId, name, city, assets[{id, siteId, type,
nickname, coverage, contractRef, requiredCertifications[]}]}]}`
`status`: active ×12, on_hold ×1 (CUS-074). **No email or domain field anywhere.**

**agreement** (13, `?route=agreements`) — flat:
`{id, customerId, status, serviceMode, responseHours, effectiveFrom, effectiveTo, supersedes?, note?}`
`status`: active ×12, suspended ×1. `serviceMode`: onsite ×12, remote_only ×1.
`responseHours`: 2, 4, 6, 8, 12.

**technician** (13) — `{id, name, city, skills[], certifications[], available, currentAssignment?}`
Cities: Bengaluru ×11, Mysuru ×1, Tumakuru ×1. 8 available / 5 not.

**request** (18, `?route=requests`) — `{id, requestId, receivedAt, channel, priority, sender{name,email},
subject, body, attachments[{id,name,type,summary}], workflow}`
Two fields the POST input schema does NOT carry: `priority` (low/normal/high/urgent) and
`attachments[].summary` (pre-summarised text — no OCR needed). `workflow` is `null` on all 18.

**work order, active** (4, `?route=work-orders`) — **snake_case, unlike every other route**:
`{id, request_id, customer_id, site_id, asset_id, technician_id, status, summary, created_at, source}`

**work-order history** (24) — camelCase:
`{id, requestId, customerId, siteId, assetId, category, summary, status, openedAt, closedAt}`
`status`: completed ×21, closed_after_review ×2, remote_resolution ×1.

## Answers to "open / to verify"

**1. covered_action vs dispatch_ready** — data supports your reading, with a sharper line.
The two `covered_action` runner cases (VIS-001 scheduled quarterly service, VIS-008 coverage
confirmation) are both *planned/administrative* work; `dispatch_ready` (VIS-006) is a
*breakdown* — "has stopped cooling". Discriminator is breakdown-vs-planned, not coverage.
Note VIS-001 is covered, has an available tech (TECH-01/08) and still expects `covered_action`
— so **availability alone must not promote planned work to dispatch**.

**2. How a business duplicate is found** — not via saved workflow state. `workflow` is `null`
on all 18 seeded requests, including VIS-001 which VIS-005 duplicates. So the only evidence
is: (a) `?route=requests` (full list) matched on asset + time proximity + body cross-reference,
and/or (b) the pre-existing open WO. Note the runner POSTs cases in order, so VIS-001 is
processed before VIS-005, but it arrives as a POST — your own store is the reliable record.
**`q=` is ignored on this route** (see traps), so filter client-side.

**3. Writing to request-workflow** — the API ref documents the workflow record and all 18 are
`null`, i.e. nothing has populated them. It is a documented POST and plausibly an observed
side effect, but it is a write and you said no POSTs yet. Fields line up with the case result
(`safetyOutcome`, `coverageOutcome`, `coordinatorNotes`, `customerReplyDraft`). Flagged for
your decision — untested.

**4. What CON-012 base says, does an A1 exist** — **neither exists.** See below; this is the
biggest correction to the notes.

**5. submission.json manifest schema** — not found. Not in the resources, not served by any
read route. Still open; likely in the workspace UI.

## Corrections / additions to the notes

**Agreement "families" do not exist in this data.** Exactly 13 agreements, one per customer,
no base contracts and no intermediate amendments. `q=CON-012` returns only `CON-012-A2`;
`q=CON-129` returns only `CON-129-A1`. CON-044-**A3** exists with no A1/A2 and no `supersedes`.
`supersedes` appears on only 2 of 13 records (CON-012-A2 → CON-012, CON-129-A1 → CON-129) and
points at a record that is **not retrievable**.
Consequence: there is no base-vs-amendment conflict to resolve at runtime — the one in-force
record per customer already carries the final `responseHours` and `serviceMode`. Build
"latest in force by date + status" as a general selector over whatever the family returns
(correct per policy, handles hidden cases), but do **not** make a resolvable base contract a
precondition — a missing `supersedes` target is normal here, not a reason for account review.
VIS-008 ("use the amendment, not the base contract") is satisfied by citing CON-012-A2 and its
4-hour window.

**Identity cannot be resolved by sender domain.** Customer records have no email field, and
`q=` on customers matches **name and aliases only** — `asterwarehousing.in`, `Whitefield`,
`AST-101` and `Main DG` all return 0 results. The Aster collision is real (CUS-012 Aster
Warehousing, CUS-019 Aster Clinical Services, both Bengaluru/Whitefield). In practice the
reliable path is **asset ID → customer**, by fetching customers and indexing assets locally;
asset IDs are globally unique across the dataset. Domain is a corroborating signal at best,
and you cannot verify it against any record.

for any query (18 and 4 respectively) and return HTTP 200 — no error, no empty set. Only

  fully instrumented in the data.

2026-09-20 request dates). Date arithmetic must run against `receivedAt`, as you planned.
